beats.text: Quentin Tarantino's film school was a video store.
A high school dropout, he spent five years behind the counter at Video Archives in Manhattan Beach, California.
The job was talking movies, with customers, and with a co-worker named Roger Avary.
Though he says he was already a movie expert. That's how he got hired.
Then came Reservoir Dogs. And Pulp Fiction: the Palme d'Or, and a screenplay Oscar he shared with Avary.
When the store closed, Tarantino bought its tapes. He's put his collection at close to eight thousand tapes and DVDs.
But here's the twist. The video store clerk now owns two Los Angeles cinemas, the New Beverly and the Vista.
Their rule? Film prints only. No digital.
He came up on tape. Now he's keeping film running.
